# vela3-fast

The default decision model. A CPU-friendly encoder with trained adapters for every built-in routing question, calibrated thresholds, and spans for PII and hallucination checks.

| Property | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Repository | [`vllm-sr/vela3-fast`](https://huggingface.co/vllm-sr/vela3-fast), pinned at `7cbefd4b92b5` |
| Family | [Vela 3.0](model-runtime/supported-models/vela-3/overview.md) |
| Parameters | 1.52B loaded |
| Backbone | UltraBERT |
| Precision (`--dtype auto`) | FP32 on every device |
| Weights | about 6.1 GB at FP32 |
| Device memory | 12 GiB or more |
| Reads | text |

## Question types

| Type | Answers |
| --- | --- |
| `choice` | Yes |
| `noul` | Yes |
| `score` | No |
| `set` | Yes, asked as one `noul` per label |
| `span` | Yes, on the `router` span head |

## Built-in questions

The Vela 3.0 family was trained on the Router's built-in
questions, so the Router asks each one in its trained form; the
[support matrix](system-one/reference/support-matrix.md) lists which.

A rule without a `predicate` takes this model's calibrated threshold:

| Preset | Threshold |
| --- | ---: |
| jailbreak (`jailbreak`) | 0.88 |
| domain (`domain`) | 0.41 |
| pii (`pii`) | 0.18 |
| fact check (`fact_check`) | 0.9999 |
| user feedback (`feedback`) | 0.47 |
| safety (`harm`) | 0.52 |
| modality (`modality`) | 0.63 |

## Hardware

Each time it loads, the model compares its answers with the reference
answers recorded for its revision. They are recorded for:

- CPU (`cpu`)
- x86-64 CPU with AVX2 (BF16 emulated) (`cpu:x86_64:avx2:bf16_emulated`)

Where a hardware reference and its device class's are both recorded, the
hardware one is checked.

On an AMD GPU or an NVIDIA GPU no reference is recorded, so the model serves
there with its self-check reported as `unverified`.

[Choose a model](model-runtime/get-started/choose-a-model.md#hardware) lists the
validated hardware.

## Quantization

The runtime loads no quantized packages of the Vela 3.0 family:
it runs at its published precision.

## Deploy it

Serve it on its own in Engine mode, to ask it directly:

<Tabs groupId="platform">
<TabItem value="cpu" label="CPU" default>

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3-fast --engine --platform cpu
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="rocm" label="AMD GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3-fast --engine --platform rocm
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem value="cuda" label="NVIDIA GPU">

```bash
vllm-sr serve vllm-sr/vela3-fast --engine --platform cuda
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Or make it the Router's decision model:

```yaml title="config.yaml"
global:
  model_catalog:
    deployments:
      primary:
        provider: model_runtime
        artifact: vllm-sr/vela3-fast
        device: auto
    system:
      decision_model: {deployment: primary}
```

`device: auto` takes the first validated GPU with enough free memory, else
the CPU; name `rocm:0` or `cuda:0` to pin a GPU.

To run it on another host and attach the Router to it:

```bash
vllm-srun serve vllm-sr/vela3-fast --device auto --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8100
```

Then set `endpoint: http://<host>:8100` and
`model: vela3-fast` on the deployment; see
[Attach to a runtime you run](model-runtime/deploy/connect-the-router.md#attach-to-a-runtime-you-run).
